children: Investors continued to put money into bonds even as flows into equities slowed, with U.S. equity funds recording their largest three-week outflow since January, according to BofA Global Research and EPFR.
Global bonds attracted $17.5B in the latest week, averaging about $18B a week over the past four weeks, while global equities drew $9.8B, BofA said.
The pace of equity inflows had slowed sharply, with global equities averaging $7B a week over the past three weeks, down from a $52B weekly average in July, according to BofA.
U.S. equities were a particular source of weakness, recording $3.9B of outflows in the latest week and $14.2B over the past three weeks, the biggest three-week outflow since January, BofA said.

The shift toward bonds was also visible across fixed income, with investment-grade bonds attracting $5B for a 23rd consecutive week of inflows. Government and Treasury bonds had recorded $6.6B of inflows over the past 11 weeks, while TIPS had attracted money for 32 straight weeks.
Lisa Abramowicz pointed out to the same trend on X, suggesting that rising bond yields could be starting to lure investors away from equities as stock-fund flows slow and bond inflows pick up.

BofA also noted that its private clients remained heavily allocated to equities, with stocks accounting for 66.2% of AUM, compared with 17.2% for bonds and 9.4% for cash, which was a record low cash allocation.

The latest flow data pointed to a growing contrast between the two asset classes, with bond inflows remaining strong while equity flows, particularly into U.S. stocks, had weakened significantly from their pace earlier in the year.

title: Investors shift toward bonds as equity flows slow, BofA says
